# Change Video Frame Rate

- Route: `/tools/change-video-frame-rate`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `change-video-frame-rate`

## Summary

Convert a video to 24, 25, 30 or 60 fps, drop a 60 fps clip to 30 for a smaller file, or match a project frame rate. (Video tools)

## Details

Frame rate decides how a video feels and how big it is. Film is 24 fps, European broadcast 25, most phones 30 or 60, and mixing them in one timeline causes judder. Media Manipulator resamples any video to the frame rate you need on our servers with FFmpeg, dropping or repeating frames exactly, and exports MP4. When you want more frames rather than fewer, the AI frame interpolation tool generates the in-betweens.
### What it does
- Resamples a video to any frame rate from 1 to 120 fps.
- Halves 60 fps to 30 for a much smaller file with no visible change for most content.
- Matches a project frame rate (24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 60) before importing into an editor.
- Keeps resolution, audio and duration unchanged.
### How to use it
1. Upload a video: Any common format.
2. Set the target fps: 30 is preselected.
3. Convert: FFmpeg drops or duplicates frames to match.
4. Download: Save the resampled MP4.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv
- Output: mp4, webm, mov, mkv
### Technical details
- Uses the fps filter: frames are dropped or duplicated by timestamp, so duration and audio sync are preserved exactly.
- Going up (30 to 60) duplicates frames and does not look smoother; use AI frame interpolation for real new frames.
- Going down removes data and is not reversible; keep the original.
### Use cases
- Shrink a 60 fps clip: Drop to 30 fps for email, chat or a smaller upload.
- Conform for editing: Match every clip to the project rate.
- Film look: Convert to 24 fps for a cinematic cadence.
- Broadcast delivery: Convert to 25 or 50 fps for PAL regions.
### FAQ
Q: Does the video get shorter or longer?
A: No. Duration is preserved; frames are dropped or repeated to hit the new rate.
Q: Will 30 to 60 fps look smoother?
A: Not with this tool, which duplicates frames. Use AI frame interpolation to generate real in-between frames.
Q: What frame rate should I pick?
A: 30 fps for most web and phone content, 24 for a film look, 25 or 50 for PAL broadcast, 60 for gaming and sports.
Q: Is the audio affected?
A: No. The audio stream is copied or re-encoded at the same timing.
